n12a04be5b6f.s: UN specialised agencies, autonomous bodies with their own treaties and budgets, are linked to which UN organ?
n12a04be5b6f.x: Specialised agencies are autonomous, with their own treaties and budgets, and are linked to ECOSOC; creation by the General Assembly with voluntary funding describes funds and programmes.

nac4a4f26cbd.s: The UNHCR, set up in 1950 for refugee protection, is classified as:
o: An Office of the General Assembly
A specialised agency linked to ECOSOC
A related organisation reporting to the UNSC
A financial institution of the World Bank Group
nac4a4f26cbd.x: UNHCR (1950, Geneva) is an Office of the General Assembly for refugee protection, not a specialised agency.

n1591a03836a.s: UNICEF, founded in 1946, is headquartered at:
n1591a03836a.x: UNICEF was founded in 1946 and its headquarters is in New York, not Geneva.

n01210833e81.s: Which pair of ILO Fundamental Conventions has India not ratified?
n01210833e81.x: India has not ratified C87 (Freedom of Association) and C98 (Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining); the other pairs are ratified.

na077c575233.s: The ILO's tripartite structure operates in the International Labour Conference and the:
na077c575233.x: The ILO's tripartite bodies are the International Labour Conference and the Governing Body, not ECOSOC.

n96854ef36f2.s: The World Food Programme (WFP) received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
n96854ef36f2.x: WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020, not 2019; OPCW won in 2013 and IPCC with Al Gore in 2007.

n30d55ace01e.s: Which arrangement filled the gap left by the never-created International Trade Organization from 1947 until 1995?
n30d55ace01e.x: The ITO proposed at Bretton Woods was not created; GATT filled the gap from 1947 until the WTO was set up in 1995.

n1efa101f222.s: Which World Bank Group institution settles investment disputes and does not have India as a member?
n1efa101f222.x: ICSID settles investment disputes, and India is not a member; MIGA insures against political risk.

n88c2390791f.s: The International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) was established in:
n88c2390791f.x: ICSID was established in 1966, not 1976; IFC dates from 1956 and MIGA from 1988.

n14678a27f02.s: IMF quotas determine a member's financial contribution, its access to borrowing and its:
n14678a27f02.x: Quotas determine contribution, borrowing access and voting power; they do not fix exchange rates.

na2411a5e8f8.s: The Andhra Pradesh Rural Roads Project is funded by:
na2411a5e8f8.x: The AP Rural Roads Project is funded by AIIB; the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is ADB-funded and the post-Hudhud Disaster Recovery Project World Bank-funded.

n764b9c945f9.s: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration (2026) noted that the Global North, with about 15% of the population, holds about what share of votes in the IMF and World Bank?
n764b9c945f9.x: The declaration demanded quota and voting reform because the Global North, with about 15% of the population, holds about 60% of the votes.

nae4ea49a43c.s: The World Trade Organization is headquartered at:
nae4ea49a43c.x: The WTO is headquartered at Geneva, not Vienna.

n2d537e10422.s: Which WTO principle gives developing countries bargaining space in negotiations?
o: Voting weighted by share of world trade
n2d537e10422.x: The WTO follows one-country-one-vote with consensus, which gives developing countries bargaining room.

nbd051a5c342.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the WTO Ministerial Conference?
o: MC13 was held at Geneva in 2022
It must meet at least once every two years
MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, in March 2026
MC12 was held at Geneva in 2022
nbd051a5c342.x: MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi in February 2024; Geneva 2022 was MC12.

n9c4565c9b59.s: The 2020 proposal for a COVID-19 TRIPS waiver was made jointly by India and:
n9c4565c9b59.x: The proposal (2020) came from India and South Africa, not Brazil; MC12 (2022) adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents.

n6e2986d1481.s: At the WTO, the US wants to deny Special and Differential Treatment to China, India, Brazil and:
n6e2986d1481.x: The US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia; India defends SDT.

n5accf91798f.s: Besides the e-commerce moratorium, what else lapsed at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference (Yaoundé, March 2026)?
o: The Peace Clause on public stockholding
n5accf91798f.x: Both the e-commerce moratorium and the TRIPS non-violation moratorium lapsed at MC14; no permanent solution on public stockholding was reached.

new.s: The Universal Postal Union (UPU), founded in 1874, is headquartered at:
new.x: The UPU (1874) is headquartered at Bern.

new.s: Which of the following UN bodies is headquartered at Rome?
new.x: WFP is in Rome (with FAO and IFAD); the ILO, WHO and ITU are in Geneva.

new.s: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is headquartered at:
new.x: ICAO (1947) is headquartered at Montreal; London hosts the IMO.

new.s: The oldest of the following UN specialised agencies, founded in 1865, is the:
new.x: The ITU dates from 1865 (International Telegraph Union); the UPU from 1874, the ILO from 1919 and WIPO from 1967.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of agency and founding year is correctly matched?
new.x: IFAD was founded in 1977. WIPO dates from 1967, IMO from 1948 and WFP from 1961.

new.s: Which UN body is both a specialised agency and an international financial institution for the rural poor?
new.x: IFAD is both a specialised agency and an international financial institution; WFP, UNDP and UNICEF are funds and programmes.

new.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is built jointly by OPHI and:
new.x: UNDP co-builds the Global MPI with OPHI (2010).

new.s: Besides UNEP, which UN body is headquartered at Nairobi?
new.x: Nairobi hosts UNEP and UN-Habitat; IFAD and WFP are in Rome.

new.s: The State of World Population report and population issues are the mandate of:
new.x: UNFPA deals with population and publishes the State of World Population.

new.s: Who became Director-General of UNESCO on 15 November 2025, the first Arab to hold the post?
new.x: Khaled El-Enany of Egypt became UNESCO DG on 15 November 2025, the first Arab DG.

new.s: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, serving a second term to August 2027, is the Director-General of:
new.x: Tedros is WHO Director-General, his second term running to 15 August 2027.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's roles in UN bodies:
1. Dr Harsh Vardhan chaired the WHO Executive Board in 2020-21.
2. Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body in 2020-21.
3. India chaired UNODC in March 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India chaired the 68th session of the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, not UNODC.

new.s: The ILO Domestic Workers Convention (C189), which India has not ratified, was adopted in:
new.x: C189 on domestic workers was adopted in 2011 and India has not ratified it.

new.s: India ratified the ILO conventions on Minimum Age (C138) and Worst Forms of Child Labour (C182) in:
new.x: India ratified C138 and C182 in 2017.

new.s: According to the ILO-UNICEF estimate released in 2025, the number of child labourers in 2024 was about:
new.x: Child labour fell from 160 million (2020) to about 138 million (2024, released 2025).

new.s: The Human Development Report is published by:
new.x: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report and builds the Global MPI with OPHI.

new.s: The World Employment and Social Outlook is published by:
new.x: The World Employment and Social Outlook is an ILO report.

new.s: According to SOFI 2026, global hunger fell for the third year to about:
new.x: SOFI 2026 reported hunger falling for the third year to 7.8% (645 million).

new.s: Which of the following was placed on India's Tentative List for World Heritage in 2022?
new.x: Lepakshi in Andhra Pradesh was placed on India's Tentative List in 2022; the others are inscribed World Heritage sites.

new.s: The Bhagavad Gita manuscripts and the Natyashastra are inscribed on UNESCO's:
new.x: The Bhagavad Gita manuscripts and the Natyashastra are on the Memory of the World register.

new.s: Deepavali was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in December 2025 at a Committee session held at:
new.x: Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th Intergovernmental Committee at the Red Fort in December 2025.

new.s: The International Labour Organization won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
new.x: The ILO won in 1969; UNICEF in 1965, UNHCR in 1954 and UN Peacekeeping Forces in 1988.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of Nobel Peace Prize winner and year is correctly matched?
new.x: UN Peacekeeping Forces won in 1988. The UN with Kofi Annan won in 2001, IPCC with Al Gore in 2007 and UNICEF in 1965.

new.s: World Food Day, 16 October, marks the founding date of:
new.x: World Food Day (16 October) is the FAO's founding date.

new.s: World Refugee Day, linked to the UNHCR, is observed on:
new.x: World Refugee Day is 20 June; 5 June is World Environment Day, 21 June Yoga Day and 7 April World Health Day.

new.s: The IMF began its operations on:
new.x: The IMF was founded in 1944, came into formal existence on 27 December 1945 and began operations on 1 March 1947.

new.s: The IMF came into formal existence, with 29 members, on:
new.x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945 with 29 members.

new.s: The Bretton Woods Conference of July 1944 was attended by delegates from how many allied nations?
new.x: 730 delegates from 44 allied nations attended the conference.

new.s: The first country to borrow from the IMF, on 8 May 1947, was:
new.x: France was the first IMF borrower, on 8 May 1947.

new.s: The Bretton Woods Conference was held at the Mount Washington Hotel in which US state?
new.x: The conference met at the Mount Washington Hotel, Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA.

new.s: Which World Bank Group institution deals with private-sector investment and conceived the 'Doing Business' report?
new.x: The IFC (1956) handles private-sector investment and advisory work and conceived 'Doing Business'.

new.s: The IBRD mainly lends to:
o: The poorest countries as interest-free credits
new.x: IBRD lends to middle-income governments; IDA gives interest-free credits to the poorest, IFC serves the private sector and MIGA insures political risk.

new.s: Who was the first woman chief economist of the IMF (2019)?
new.x: Gita Gopinath became the IMF's first woman chief economist in 2019.

new.s: Who was the first President of the New Development Bank (2015)?
new.x: K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President (2015).

new.s: Who was the IMF's youngest chief economist, during 2003-06?
new.x: Raghuram Rajan was the IMF's youngest chief economist (2003-06).

new.s: Masato Kanda, from February 2025, is the 11th President of:
new.x: Masato Kanda became the 11th ADB President in February 2025; the ADB President is traditionally Japanese.

new.s: After the quota reform effective 25 November 2024, India's rank by IMF quota is:
new.x: India's IMF quota is about 2.75% (votes about 2.63%), 8th by quota.

new.s: Which country became the 191st member of the IMF on 21 October 2024?
new.x: Liechtenstein became the IMF's 191st member on 21 October 2024.

new.s: The IMF's regular review of each member's economy is known as:
new.x: Article IV consultations are the IMF's regular reviews of each member's economy; the others are lending facilities.

new.s: Which body advises the IMF Board of Governors?
new.x: The International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC) advises the IMF Board of Governors.

new.s: The World Economic Outlook is published by:
new.x: The World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report and Fiscal Monitor are IMF reports.

new.s: The Global Economic Prospects report, issued every January and June, is published by:
new.x: Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank report (January and June).

new.s: Which of the following pairs of report and institution is correctly matched?
o: Global Financial Stability Report – World Bank
new.x: The World Development Report is a World Bank report; Fiscal Monitor and the GFSR are IMF reports and Global Economic Prospects is the World Bank's.

new.s: The New Development Bank's regional office in India is located at:
new.x: NDB regional offices are at Johannesburg, São Paulo, GIFT City (India) and Moscow.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. Its founders hold equal votes and no one has a veto.
2. It is headquartered at Shanghai.
3. It is open only to BRICS members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NDB is open to all UN members.

new.s: The two largest shareholders of the Asian Development Bank are:
new.x: Japan and the USA are the largest ADB shareholders (about 15.6% each); India is 4th.

new.s: India's rank among shareholders of the Asian Development Bank is:
new.x: India is the ADB's 4th-largest shareholder (about 6.3%).

new.s: The newest member of the Asian Development Bank (2025) is:
new.x: The ADB has 69 members; Türkiye joined as the newest in 2025.

new.s: The largest shareholder of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is:
new.x: China is the largest AIIB shareholder (about 26.5% of votes); India is second (about 7.6%).

new.s: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is headquartered at:
new.x: AIIB is headquartered at Beijing; Shanghai hosts the NDB and Manila the ADB.

new.s: How many approved members did the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank have in September 2026?
new.x: AIIB had 111 approved members in September 2026; the ADB has 69.

new.s: Phase I of the Amaravati capital project is funded by:
new.x: The World Bank (IBRD) and ADB fund Amaravati Phase I with $800 million each ($1.6 billion).

new.s: The post-Hudhud Andhra Pradesh Disaster Recovery Project is funded by:
new.x: The AP Disaster Recovery Project after Cyclone Hudhud is World Bank-funded.

new.s: As of March 2026, the World Trade Organization had how many members?
new.x: The WTO had 166 members in March 2026, the latest being Comoros and Timor-Leste (2024).

new.s: Which two countries are the latest members of the WTO, having joined in 2024?
new.x: Comoros and Timor-Leste joined the WTO in 2024.

new.s: The first WTO Ministerial Conference (1996) was held at:
new.x: MC1 was held at Singapore in 1996; Seattle (1999) and Cancún (2003) broke down.

new.s: Which WTO body runs the organisation between Ministerial Conferences and also sits as the DSB and TPRB?
new.x: The General Council runs the WTO between MCs and also sits as the Dispute Settlement Body and Trade Policy Review Body.

new.s: The WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (February 2024) was held at:
new.x: MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024); MC12 was at Geneva and MC14 at Yaoundé.

new.s: The WTO agreement on trade-distorting investment measures such as local content rules is:
new.x: TRIMS covers trade-distorting investment measures like local content; TRIPS covers IPR and GATS services.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of WTO agreement and subject is correctly matched?
o: TBT – Food safety, animal and plant health
TRIMS – Minimum standards for all IPR
new.x: GATS covers trade in services. SPS covers food safety and plant health, TBT technical regulations and TRIPS IPR standards.

new.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which box of support has no limit?
new.x: Green Box support is non- or minimally trade-distorting and has no limit; Amber Box support is capped.

new.s: The de minimis limit of trade-distorting farm support for developing countries under the AoA is:
new.x: De minimis is 10% of production for developing countries and 5% for developed ones.

new.s: The WTO Peace Clause shielding developing-country public stockholding was agreed at:
new.x: The Peace Clause was agreed at Bali in 2013; a 2014 decision extended it until a permanent solution.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Amber Box support is trade-distorting and capped.
2. Blue Box support is Amber Box support with production limits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Amber Box covers trade-distorting support such as price support and is capped; Blue Box is Amber support with production limits.

new.s: India's first compulsory licence under its patent law, in the Natco-Bayer case, was granted in:
new.x: The first compulsory licence (Natco-Bayer) came in 2012; the Patents Act was amended in 2005.

new.s: To meet its TRIPS obligations, India amended its Patents Act in:
new.x: The Patents Act was amended in 2005; the GI Act was passed in 1999.

new.s: The WTO case against India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ) was brought by:
new.x: The USA, not the EU, challenged MEIS and SEZ; a panel ruled against India in 2019.

new.s: India's sugar subsidies were challenged at the WTO by Brazil, Australia and:
new.x: Brazil, Australia and Guatemala challenged India's sugar subsidies; the panel ruled against India in Dec 2021.

new.s: The WTO dispute over India's solar panel domestic-content rules under JNNSM, which India lost in 2016, was brought by:
new.x: The USA brought the solar panels case; India lost in 2016.

new.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions had been in force since:
new.x: The e-commerce moratorium ran from 1998 until it lapsed on 31 March 2026.

new.s: Phase 2 of the WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations, unresolved at MC14, deals with:
new.x: Fisheries Phase 2 deals with overcapacity and overfishing and was unresolved at MC14.

new.s: The first Anti-Dumping Code was an outcome of which GATT round?
new.x: The Kennedy Round (1964-67) produced tariff cuts and the first Anti-Dumping Code.

new.s: The Doha Development Agenda, which later stalled, was launched in:
new.x: The Doha Development Agenda began in 2001 and stalled.
